items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: The interviewee mentions Reed Vaughn only in the context of the interviewer's story about Lou Dillon teaching Reed. The interviewee does not claim to have met, worked with, or known Reed Vaughn personally.

ctx.x: Yeah. By the way, Joe Burton, even though he wasn't a great player, was responsible for getting some of the best bass players and drummers work in town. Reed worked with him quite a while. James Black worked with him quite a while. Charlie, you worked with him, didn't you?
Yeah. Well, he drove all the better drummers away because by that time I was into my English teaching career and he pissed them off so badly that they wouldn't work with him anymore.
